## Research question

::: {.small .muted}
**Current version:** *To what extent has immigration-related population growth been associated with increasing housing demand, supply shortages and rising housing prices in Spain between 2015 and 2025?*
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Proposal"}
**Is immigration-driven population growth associated with faster growth in housing prices and rents across Spanish provinces, and is this association stronger where new construction lagged behind?**
:::

- **H1:** provinces with more immigration see faster price and rent growth
- **H2:** the effect is larger where new housing did not keep up

::: {.small .muted}
Business angle: returns for **landlords and investors**, response of **construction**.
:::

::: notes
Goal of the meeting: leave with the final question. Three changes from her version: one outcome block (prices and rents) instead of three; a unit of analysis (provinces, or regions if the data are not available); the supply side as a test (H2), not as a separate outcome. Period: 2015 to the latest year available, probably 2023 or 2024 for rents. Say "associated", not "caused": migrants also move to regions that are already booming.
:::

## Model and data

ΔPrice~pt~ = β·Immig~pt~ + γ·(Immig~pt~ × Supply~pt~) + α~p~ + τ~t~ + ε~pt~

::: {.small .muted}
Province *p*, year *t*. α~p~: fixed differences between provinces. τ~t~: national shocks (interest rates, COVID).
:::

| Variable | Source |
|---|---|
| Foreign-born population | INE, *Padrón continuo* |
| House prices | INE price index; Ministry of Housing |
| Rents | Ministry of Housing rental index (SERPAVI) |
| New construction | Ministry of Housing: permits, completions |
| Controls | INE: unemployment, income |

::: notes
H1 is beta, H2 is gamma. Immig: growth in the foreign-born population relative to the previous year's total population. Supply: completions or permits relative to population growth. About 50 provinces x 9-10 years = 450-500 observations, enough for a fixed-effects regression. Check coverage first: SERPAVI ends earlier than the other series. Endogeneity goes in the limitations; a shift-share instrument (Card 2001) can be mentioned as future research. Software to agree: Stata, R or Gretl.
:::
